# Run pnpm env:prepare to create a protected .env with fresh local credentials.
# This template contains no usable credentials. Review local settings afterward.
# Browser-reachable API origin for authentication and rendered media.
LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000/
# Host-side Astro export transport. Compose builder overrides this internally.
LACE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000/
LACE_DATABASE_PATH=./.lace/data/lace.sqlite
# Empty trusts only the TCP peer. Set only the CIDRs of your controlled ingress proxies.
# See docs/lace-compose-production.md for trusted client identity and network isolation.
LACE_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS=
# Optional Cloudflare operator target settings:
LACE_D1_DATABASE_ID=
LACE_CLOUDFLARE_PERSIST_TO=
CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=
LACE_WRANGLER_CONFIG=
LACE_API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/api:0.1.0-rc2
LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/lacecms/builder:0.1.0-rc2
LACE_AUTH_SECRET=
LACE_MINIO_ROOT_ACCESS_KEY=
LACE_MINIO_ROOT_SECRET=
LACE_MINIO_BUCKET=lace-media
LACE_MINIO_REGION=us-east-1
LACE_MINIO_TIMEOUT_MS=5000
LACE_BUILDER_SECRET=
# Leave empty until Admin Settings issues a read-only build token.
LACE_BUILD_TOKEN=
LACE_API_PORT=3000
LACE_HTTP_PORT=8080
# Optional transactional email. Leave LACE_EMAIL_PROVIDER empty to disable it.
# smtp (STARTTLS or TLS) or resend; check with Admin Settings > Send test email.
# See docs/lace-operations.md#email-delivery. Never commit passwords or API keys.
LACE_EMAIL_PROVIDER=
LACE_EMAIL_FROM=
LACE_SMTP_HOST=
LACE_SMTP_PORT=587
LACE_SMTP_SECURITY=starttls
LACE_SMTP_USER=
LACE_SMTP_PASSWORD=
LACE_RESEND_API_KEY=

# Build source host mount; site/output directories are relative inside the container.
LACE_BUILD_SOURCE_ROOT=.
LACE_BUILD_SITE_DIR=site
LACE_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR=dist
LACE_BUILD_SITE_ID=main-site
LACE_BUILD_SITE_LABEL="Main site"
# Optional public site base URL, e.g. https://example.com/. The editor links published
# entries to it ("Open on site") and site builds use it for canonical URLs, og:url and
# sitemap.xml; leave it empty to show paths as text and build without a sitemap.
LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL=
# Site indexing: empty or on lets search engines index the site; off (staging, previews)
# marks every page noindex and makes robots.txt disallow everything.
LACE_SITE_INDEXING=

# Optional public API reference at /api/docs (browser needs jsDelivr access).
# LACE_API_DOCS_ENABLED=true

# Optional content assistant; apply database migrations before enabling.
# MCP allows read/create/save-draft; publishing needs separate content:publish consent.
# Unpublishing and deletion remain unavailable.
LACE_MCP_ENABLED=false

FROM golang:1.23.6-bookworm AS build

ARG MINIO_TAG=RELEASE.2025-02-07T23-21-09Z
ARG MINIO_COMMIT=703f51164d3d0c44af41b0d86075a1f61e4779e7
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "$MINIO_TAG" https://github.com/minio/minio.git /src \
    && test "$(git -C /src rev-parse HEAD)" = "$MINIO_COMMIT"
WORKDIR /src
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath \
    -ldflags "$(go run buildscripts/gen-ldflags.go)" \
    -o /minio .

FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=build /minio /usr/local/bin/minio
EXPOSE 9000 9001
ENTRYPOINT ["minio"]
CMD ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]

# Connect an existing Astro site Use this guide when your Astro site already exists and the Lace CMS lives in a subdirectory generated with `pnpm create lace@0.1.0-rc2 cms`. The CMS never modifies your site; every file below is yours. For build-site selection, mounts and the Compose builder, see [Selecting the build site](lace-operations.md#selecting-the-build-site). ```text my-site/ your Astro project (lockfile root) ├── cms/ generated Lace project ├── lace.site.json Lace block lock (step 5) └── src/ ├── components/lace/ block components (step 5) ├── lace/blocks.ts block map (step 5) ├── lib/lace.ts loader file (step 3) └── pages/ your routes (step 6) ``` ## 1. Install the Lace site packages Astro `^7.3.1` must already be a dependency. In the site root: ```sh pnpm add @lacecms/astro@0.1.0-rc2 @lacecms/render@0.1.0-rc2 @lacecms/sdk@0.1.0-rc2 @lacecms/content@0.1.0-rc2 sharp@0.35.5 ``` `@lacecms/sdk` loads published content, `@lacecms/render` validates blocks and rich text with the CMS rules, `@lacecms/astro` renders them in Astro, and `@lacecms/content` provides the built-in block definitions. Upgrade all four together. `sharp` is the image library Astro uses for the block image variants (section 12). ## 2. Configure the server-only environment Set these for `astro dev` and `astro build` (for example in the site's ignored `.env`); never prefix them with `PUBLIC_`: | Variable | Value | | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `LACE_API_BASE_URL` | Origin of the Lace API that serves the published build export | | `LACE_BUILD_TOKEN` | Read-only build token created in Admin Settings | | `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Browser-facing API origin for media URLs (defaults to `LACE_API_BASE_URL`) | | `LACE_EXPECTED_PUBLISHED_VERSION` | Optional; the Compose builder sets it so a build fails if content changes mid-build | | `LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL` | Optional public site base URL; enables canonical URLs, `og:url` and `sitemap.xml` | | `LACE_SITE_INDEXING` | Optional `on` (default) or `off`; `off` keeps staging builds out of search engines | The token is read only in server code and never reaches the browser. ## 3. Create the loader file `src/lib/lace.ts`: ```ts import { createAstroSiteLoader } from "@lacecms/astro"; const onLinkDiagnostics = (diagnostics: import("@lacecms/sdk").LinkDiagnostics) => { if (diagnostics.total > 0) console.warn("[lace] Unavailable internal links", diagnostics); }; export const getSite = createAstroSiteLoader({ onLinkDiagnostics, env: { ...import.meta.env, ...process.env }, dev: import.meta.env.DEV, }); ``` A static build reads one export for all routes; `astro dev` revalidates it on every request so publications appear on reload. Pass `hints` to append your own instructions to configuration, token or connection errors. ## 4. Let TypeScript read `.astro` imports `src/env.d.ts`: ```ts /// // Lets `tsc` type `.astro` imports in TypeScript modules such as the block map. declare module "*.astro" { const component: (props: Record) => unknown; export default component; } ``` ## 5. Add the block components From the `cms/` directory, install the block components, the block map and the block lock into your site: ```sh pnpm exec lace add block --all --site .. ``` `--all` installs a component for every block type `cms/lace.config.ts` registers; name types instead (`lace add block hero cta --site ..`) to install only those. The command writes `src/components/lace/*Block.astro`, `src/lace/blocks.ts` and `lace.site.json` in the site, and prints the exact `pnpm --dir .. add ...` command when a required Lace package is missing or outdated; it never edits your `package.json` or other source. Use `--dry-run` to review the plan without writing. The components are your source: change their markup and styles freely. Each receives `block`, validated `data`, `context`, `mediaUrl` and `image`; rich-text fields render through `@lacecms/astro/RichText.astro`. `image(mediaId, usageAlt?)` describes a media field for an ``: `src`, the effective `alt` (the usage alt text such as the image block's `alt`, else the media item's alt text from the Media library, else `""`), `width` and `height` to prevent layout shift, `caption`, and `objectPosition` (for example `25% 40%`) from the focal point set in Media. A media ID missing from the build export fails the build with its block. Outside blocks, `site.media(id)` and `site.image(id, usageAlt?)` (also available on each entry) return the resolved media item. A block type that is missing from the map fails the build with its model, entry and block key. Running the command again after a CLI upgrade updates only files you have not changed; an edited component or block map is reported as a conflict with a diff and left untouched (`--write-new` writes the proposed file next to it as `.new`). For a custom block, export its `defineBlock` value from a module that `lace.config.ts` imports, record that module path relative to the site root as `"definitions"` in `lace.site.json`, then run `pnpm exec lace add block --site ..` to scaffold a typed component with the styling hooks and register it in the block map. Editors can give a block an in-page anchor, an extra CSS class name and the settings its definition declares, and can hide it. Components also receive `anchor` and `className` when the block has them, and `settings` with every declared default applied. Place the anchor as the `id` of the component's root element and merge the class name into its `class`; Astro leaves out an `undefined` attribute, so a block without them renders unchanged: ```astro --- import type { BlockProps } from "@lacecms/render"; import type * as definitions from "../../../cms/lace.blocks"; type Props = BlockProps; const { anchor, block, className, data, settings } = Astro.props; ---

{data.message}

``` Declare settings beside the fields with the `select`, `boolean`, `number` or `text` builders, each with a `defaultValue`; `settings` is then typed with every declared key present. Settings are part of the block definition, so adding or changing one needs a version increase and a migration, which receives and returns `{ data, settings }`: ```ts export const banner = defineBlock({ type: "banner", version: 1, fields: { message: field.text({ required: true }) }, settings: { tone: field.select({ options: ["info", "warning"], defaultValue: "info" }), }, }); ``` Anchors are unique within one entry, so a link such as `#pricing` in a URL or rich-text field reaches the block on that entry's page; keep anchors distinct yourself when a page renders blocks of several entries, such as a global. A hidden block stays in Admin and in the published entry but is never delivered: the build export leaves it out and `LaceBlocks` never renders it. An invalid anchor, class name or settings value fails the build with `invalid_block_envelope` and its block. Two built-in blocks hold repeatable content in group and list fields; editors fill them with the generic Add, Remove, Duplicate and reorder controls and must add at least one item before publishing: - `gallery` (version 5) has an optional `title` and up to 50 `images`. Each item has a `kind`: an `image` item has `media`, an optional `alt`, `caption` and `link`; a `video` item has a YouTube or Vimeo `videoUrl`, a `videoTitle`, `playback` (`player` or `ambient`), `aspectRatio` and an optional `caption`. Editors add images with **Add** and videos with **Add Video**. `GalleryBlock.astro` renders a `
` with a list of figures. Each image uses `image(item.media, item.alt)`, so its alt text falls back to the media item's alt text and then to `""`; the caption falls back to the media caption. Images carry `width`, `height`, the focal-point `object-position` and `loading="lazy"`. Video items render the player in their cell, sized by `GalleryVideo.css`, with the same ambient, reduced-motion and no-JavaScript behavior as the Video embed block. Published items include only the fields of their kind, so a customized copy checks `item.kind` and that `item.media` is present before describing an image. - Upgrading from template 0.44.0: raise the version of every model that allows `gallery` and run `pnpm content:sync`. Before the next build, update the component with `pnpm exec lace add block gallery --site site` or merge the `.new` proposals; a revision 6 component fails with `block_version_mismatch` after sync. - `navigation` has an optional `name` (the `aria-label` of its `
`; name every navigation when a page has several) and up to 20 `links`, each with a `label`, an optional `url` and up to 20 `children` (one submenu level). A link without children is an ``, or plain text without a URL. A link with children becomes a `
`/`` disclosure that opens with Enter, Space, a click or a tap without JavaScript; its own URL, if it has one, is the first link of the submenu. A root-relative link to the current page gets `aria-current="page"`. The disclosure does not close on Escape or on an outside click; add a script to your copy of the component if you need that. Links use the URL rules of every `url` field: `/path`, `#anchor`, `https://…`, `mailto:` or `tel:`. ## 6. Render a page and a collection Read entries from the published site by path, or by model and slug. Your routes should produce the paths configured in `cms/lace.config.ts` (for example `route: "/articles/:slug"`) so Admin preview links match. `src/pages/index.astro`: ```astro --- import LaceBlocks from "@lacecms/astro/LaceBlocks.astro"; import Site from "../layouts/Site.astro"; import { blocks } from "../lace/blocks"; import { getSite } from "../lib/lace"; const site = await getSite(); const home = site.byPath("/"); if (home === undefined) throw new Error("Publish the home page in Lace Admin."); const posts = site.entries("posts"); ---

``` `src/pages/articles/[slug].astro`: ```astro --- import LaceBlocks from "@lacecms/astro/LaceBlocks.astro"; import Site from "../../layouts/Site.astro"; import { blocks } from "../../lace/blocks"; import { getSite } from "../../lib/lace"; export async function getStaticPaths() { const site = await getSite(); return site.entries("posts").map((post) => ({ params: { slug: post.slug } })); } const site = await getSite(); const post = site.bySlug("posts", Astro.params.slug ?? Read site-wide content (globals) A global is a configuration-defined model with exactly one entry and no URL, such as site settings. Declare it in `cms/lace.config.ts`: ```ts defineGlobal({ key: "settings", version: 1, label: "Site settings", fields: { siteName: field.text({ label: "Site name", required: true }), tagline: field.text({ label: "Tagline" }), }, }); ``` Run configuration sync, then edit and publish it from the Site group in Admin. Publishing a global requests a site build, because any page may show it. `site.global(key)` returns the published global from the same build export, or `undefined` while it has never been published, so keep static fallbacks. A published global's `media(id)` and `image(id, usageAlt?)` resolve media like an entry's. A global can also allow blocks. Site-wide navigation is a global that allows only the `navigation` block: ```ts defineGlobal({ key: "navigation", version: 1, label: "Navigation", description: "Links shown in the header of every page.", blocks: ["navigation"], }); ``` Render its published blocks with `LaceBlocks` and the same block map as your pages, and keep static links until it is published. A published global without blocks renders no navigation: ```astro --- import LaceBlocks from "@lacecms/astro/LaceBlocks.astro"; import type { PublishedSite } from "@lacecms/sdk"; import { blocks } from "../lace/blocks"; interface Props { readonly site: PublishedSite; } const { site } = Astro.props; const navigation = site.global("navigation"); --- {navigation === undefined ? The same block can also be added to a page's content for local navigation, such as links to `#anchor` targets on that page; it shows its own links, not the global's. Anchors of global blocks are not checked against the anchors of the page, so leave the site navigation without an anchor. ## 8. Group and list fields in your models Models and block definitions can describe structured content with `field.group` (one object with named child fields) and `field.list` (an ordered array whose items share one field, a scalar or a group). For example, a page with a team section: ```ts definePage({ key: "about", version: 2, path: "/about", fields: { contact: field.group({ label: "Contact", fields: { email: field.text({ label: "Email" }), phone: field.text({ label: "Phone" }), }, }), team: field.list({ label: "Team", itemLabel: "name", maxItems: 12, item: field.group({ fields: { name: field.text({ label: "Name", required: true }), photo: field.media({ label: "Photo" }), links: field.list({ label: "Links", item: field.url() }), }, }), }), }, }); ``` Your route reads them from `entry.fields` as plain JSON (check each value, as for globals), and `entry.image(id, usageAlt?)` resolves nested media. `itemLabel` names the child field shown as each item's summary in Admin. Limits are enforced by the API and shown in the editor: - a list holds at most 100 items, or its lower `maxItems`; `minItems` and required children apply only when publishing; - one entry holds at most 500 list items in total, counting every list in its fields and in all of its blocks (hidden blocks and nested lists included): 10 groups with 20 links each count 210; - a field branch has at most six groups and lists, at most two groups directly inside each other, and no list directly inside a list (put it in a group); - nested values count toward the existing JSON size limits and the 200-media-reference limit of an entry. Changing these fields later follows the configuration sync rules: raise the model version; added children and defaults fill existing items; a child renamed in place declares `renamedFrom` with its former key, and a removed child is listed in the model's `removedFields` as a pointer where `*` stands for every list item (`"/team/*/photo"`); tightening a limit is refused while stored content exceeds it, and sync never truncates a list. Block data changes still need a block version and a migration. Media used in nested fields appears in the Media library usage list and cannot be deleted while referenced. See the operations guide for sync and backups. ## 9. Add SEO metadata, a sitemap and robots.txt Opt routable models into per-entry SEO in `cms/lace.config.ts` with `seo: true`, or name fallback fields with `seo: { description: "excerpt", image: "cover" }`; raise the model version and run configuration sync. One global may map site-wide defaults from its own fields: ```ts defineGlobal({ key: "settings", version: 2, label: "Site settings", fields: { siteName: field.text({ label: "Site name", required: true }), description: field.textarea({ label: "Site description" }), image: field.media({ label: "Share image" }), }, seoDefaults: { siteName: "siteName", description: "description", image: "image" }, }); ``` `site.seo(entry)` resolves the head metadata: the SEO title, otherwise the entry title through the title template (default `%s | {siteName}`); the SEO description, then the model's mapped field, then the site default; the same chain for the image (image media only); the SEO canonical, otherwise `LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL` plus the entry path. Render it in your layout's `` with the adapter's head component, which also writes Open Graph and `twitter:card` tags; pass `type="article"` for posts: ```astro --- import LaceSeo from "@lacecms/astro/LaceSeo.astro"; import type { PublishedEntry, PublishedSite } from "@lacecms/sdk"; interface Props { readonly entry: PublishedEntry; readonly site: PublishedSite; readonly type?: "article" | "website"; } const { entry, site, type } = Astro.props; --- ``` Add two endpoints next to your pages. A `sitemap.xml.ts` page lists every indexable published entry with `lastmod` from its publication time; pass `{ include: (entry) => ... }` to keep only entries your site has routes for: ```ts import { sitemapResponse } from "@lacecms/astro"; import { getSite } from "../lib/lace"; export async function GET(): Promise { return sitemapResponse(await getSite()); } ``` A `robots.txt.ts` page allows everything and names the sitemap: ```ts import { robotsResponse } from "@lacecms/astro"; import { getSite } from "../lib/lace"; export async function GET(): Promise { return robotsResponse(await getSite()); } ``` Without `LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL` the build warns, writes no `sitemap.xml`, and pages have no canonical URL or `og:url`. With `LACE_SITE_INDEXING=off` every page is marked `noindex, nofollow` and `robots.txt` disallows everything. Entries marked _noindex_ in Admin get `noindex, follow` and are left out of the sitemap. Crawlers read `robots.txt` only at the host root, so a site served under a path must publish its robots rules at the root itself; one sitemap holds at most 50,000 URLs. ## 10. Customize rich text `` renders only the shared Lace allowlist and never raw HTML. Pass `components` to replace the element for a node or mark; an override receives the validated element and its rendered children: ```astro --- import type { RichTextOverrideProps } from "@lacecms/astro"; type Props = RichTextOverrideProps; const { element } = Astro.props; --- ``` ```astro ``` ## 11. Style through the hooks Target `data-lace-model`, `data-lace-entry`, `data-lace-block`, `data-lace-block-key` and `data-lace-part`; tag names and incidental classes are not part of the contract. A block's `id` and its editor class name are content that editors choose and change, so style them only for classes you offer editors on purpose (and keep those classes in any CSS purge safelist): ```css /* Style Lace content only through the public data-lace-* hooks. */ [data-lace-block="hero"] [data-lace-part="heading"] { font-size: 3rem; } [data-lace-model="posts"] [data-lace-block="quote"] { border-inline-start: 4px solid currentColor; } /* Only resolved anchors get a navigation affordance; unavailable labels remain plain text. */ .link { margin-block: 1rem; } .link[data-lace-appearance="button"] [data-lace-part="link"] { display: inline-block; padding: 0.65rem 1rem; border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 0.35rem; text-decoration: none; } .link[data-lace-appearance="text"] [data-lace-part="link"] { text-decoration: underline; } .link [data-lace-part="link"]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; } ``` The gallery exposes the parts `title`, `items`, `item`, `media` and `caption`, and for video items `player` and `source` inside `[data-lace-video]`; the navigation exposes `list`, `item`, `link`, `label`, `submenu`, `toggle` and `children`. Neither component ships styles. This CSS lays galleries out as an adaptive grid that crops images around their focal point, and navigation as a vertical list on narrow screens and a row with dropdown submenus from `48rem`: ```css :where([data-lace-block="gallery"]) [data-lace-part="items"] { display: grid; gap: 1rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(14rem, 100%), 1fr)); list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } :where([data-lace-block="gallery"]) figure { margin: 0; } :where([data-lace-block="gallery"]) [data-lace-part="media"] { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; display: block; height: auto; object-fit: cover; width: 100%; } :where([data-lace-block="navigation"]) ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } :where([data-lace-block="navigation"]) [data-lace-part="list"] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; } :where([data-lace-block="navigation"]) [data-lace-part="children"] { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; margin-block-start: 0.5rem; padding-inline-start: 1rem; } @media (min-width: 48rem) { :where([data-lace-block="navigation"]) [data-lace-part="list"] { flex-flow: row wrap; gap: 0.5rem 1.5rem; } :where([data-lace-block="navigation"]) [data-lace-part="submenu"] { position: relative; } :where([data-lace-block="navigation"]) [data-lace-part="children"] { background: Canvas; border: 1px solid; inset-block-start: 100%; inset-inline-start: 0; min-width: 12rem; padding: 0.75rem; position: absolute; z-index: 1; } } ``` ## 12. Images: variants, placeholder and lightbox The `image`, `gallery` and `hero` components render media through `@lacecms/astro/LaceImage.astro`. During the build it fetches each original from the public media path under `LACE_API_BASE_URL` (the origin the build already reads the export from) and, through Astro's image pipeline, writes WebP variants 960 and 1920 pixels wide, each capped at the original width, to `dist/_astro/`. The `` lists them in `srcset` with the `sizes` the component passes, keeps the original `width` and `height`, and loads lazily with `decoding="async"`; the hero loads eagerly with `fetchpriority="high"`. Animated GIFs become animated WebP. A 64-pixel WebP of each opaque image is inlined as a blurred `background-image` until the image loads; transparent images and GIFs get none. Allow the media path as an Astro remote image: `astro.config.mjs`: ```js import { laceImageConfig } from "@lacecms/astro"; import { defineConfig } from "astro/config"; export default defineConfig({ image: laceImageConfig(process.env), output: "static" }); ``` `laceImageConfig(env)` allows exactly `/api/v1/public/media/*` and nothing without that variable. Astro does not load `.env` for its config file; the starter's `astro.config.mjs` reads the project `.env` with Node's `util.parseEnv` and overlays `process.env`. Pass `optimizeImages: false` to `createAstroSiteLoader` to render the public media URLs as before, without variants. The `image` and `gallery` blocks have an _Open full screen_ setting (off by default). When an editor turns it on, each image becomes a button that opens the original from its public URL in a modal `` with a _Close_ button; Escape and a click on the backdrop also close it. It uses HTML invoker commands and no script, so it works in Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2 and later; older browsers show the image without the action. The original is downloaded only when the dialog opens. Style it through the `lightbox-trigger`, `lightbox`, `lightbox-close` and `lightbox-media` parts (see the starter stylesheet). The `image` block and every gallery item also have an optional _Link_ (a URL field with the usual safe URL rules: site paths, `#fragments`, `http(s)`, `mailto:` and `tel:`). A linked image is wrapped in an `` that opens the link in the same tab, and it never gets a lightbox, even with _Open full screen_ on; images without a link keep the lightbox. The image's alt text names the link; when it is empty, the caption, then the URL, becomes the link's `aria-label`, so give linked images alt text that describes the destination. Style the wrapper through the `link` part (see the starter stylesheet). Astro keeps downloaded originals and variants in `node_modules/.astro/assets/` and revalidates them with the media `ETag`; Lace keeps placeholders in `node_modules/.astro/lace/placeholders/`. Keep that directory between builds to avoid downloading every original again. The Compose builder does this for you: it links the site's `node_modules/.astro` to its persistent `builder-cache` volume, together with the pnpm package store, clears the whole cache when it grows above 2 GiB and drops the Astro part after a failed build. The generated Cloudflare Pages workflow restores and saves the same directory with `actions/cache`. Variants, scripts and styles land in `dist/_astro/` with a content hash in their names, so browsers may keep them: the Compose web proxy serves `/_astro/` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000, immutable` (30 days) while pages keep revalidating. On Cloudflare Pages the starter site's `public/_headers` applies the same rule; for an existing site, add `public/_headers` with: ```text /_astro/* Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000, immutable ``` A site that changes Astro's `build.assets` directory gets no long-lived caching: its assets keep revalidating. ## 13. Build ```sh pnpm astro build ``` The build fails instead of emitting partial pages when the token is missing or rejected, the API is unreachable, a media original cannot be fetched, a block has no component, or block data or rich text breaks the CMS rules. ## Organize admin forms without changing site data Models, block data and group fields (including list-item groups) can declare `layout: { mode: "sections" | "tabs", groups: [{ key, label, description?, fields }] }`. Unlisted fields appear afterwards in declaration order. Scalars/lists do not accept layout; a list's group item does. A block's `settingsLayout` refers only to its declared settings. System title, slug, SEO and block envelope controls keep their established placement. Visual sections/tabs add no data objects, paths or defaults. Synchronize metadata as usual: public version advances and a build is requested/coalesced, without changing stored content/revisions. Deploy matching content/config/contracts/API/admin packages before adoption; remove layout options before rollback to an older engine. The collection Create entry dialog suggests an ASCII slug from title until manual editing (including clearing it); explicitly re-enable Suggest from title to resume. NFKD accents are removed (`Café` → `cafe`), separators become hyphens, and the maximum is 100 characters with no boundary hyphens. Non-Latin/empty titles have no fallback or transliteration; enter a slug manually or draft without one. Suggestions do not guarantee uniqueness; publication reports route conflicts normally. Creation saves the slug atomically and opens a clean editor. Existing entries and duplicates retain their slug until explicitly edited or the editor's opt-in suggestion control is enabled. ## Reusable list layouts (Gallery v4) Gallery imports its site-owned `ListLayout.css` companion. `lace add block gallery` installs both under the configured components directory and records both hashes in the same item. CSS/component conflicts preserve the entire active item; inspect `--dry-run` and `--write-new`, then merge and rerun instead of overwriting edits. Custom lists spread `listLayoutSettings()` from `@lacecms/content` into scalar settings, set `settingsVisibility: listLayoutSettingsVisibility()` on the block (using the companion export from `@lacecms/content`), and reuse the installed CSS by relative import. Mark their outer element `data-lace-layout-container`, list `data-lace-layout`, `data-lace-wrap` and `data-lace-preset` from validated settings, and direct items `data-lace-layout-item`. Do not claim a second registry ownership of the shared file. The `lace-layout` layer has zero-specificity structural rules; site CSS controls decoration and image crop. Set `--lace-list-gap` (default 0) and `--lace-list-item-min` (14rem). Unlayered site rules override it; order theme layers after `lace-layout` otherwise. No Gallery v4 migration, SQL migration or Astro source/CSS update is needed for visibility. ## Video embeds New starters include `videoEmbed`. Existing sites can install it with `pnpm exec lace add block videoEmbed --site site` (use your actual site path). Use matching content/render/adapter/CLI packages. Review the component and its `VideoEmbed.css` companion together; use `--dry-run` and `--write-new` to resolve local source conflicts. Register `builtInBlocks.videoEmbed`, allow the type in selected CMS models, advance their versions and run configuration sync. The block accepts YouTube watch/share/shorts/embed URLs and Vimeo video/player URLs. For example, `https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ` or an unlisted Vimeo URL `https://vimeo.com/76979871/abc123def` (substitute the owner's real privacy hash). Title is required for accessibility; poster image and caption are optional. Provider restrictions and media references are validated in the CMS. Activating it loads one iframe and moves focus there; playback never autostarts and can need a second click on Play. No provider requests or thumbnails are loaded before that activation. URL playback/tracking parameters are not forwarded; only a Vimeo privacy hash is retained. The renderer is site-owned. It is the sole built-in with a small local activation and ambient mounting script; there is no provider SDK or framework hydration. `VideoEmbed.css` reserves the selected responsive aspect ratio (16:9 by default) in `@layer lace-layout`; site CSS owns decoration. Hooks: `data-lace-part="preview|play|player|caption|source"` on the corresponding elements. `describeVideoEmbed` from `@lacecms/render` supplies canonical player data without network access. Adding allowed Link blocks or optional model/global URL fields needs model version increments and normal sync; existing block schema versions stay unchanged. The Link block's button/text appearance styles belong to your site. The new API exports format 2 with required local `internalLinks` manifests; format-1-only SDKs reject it. A current loader accepts formats 1 and 2, resolves only after every export page and exposes bounded `linkDiagnostics` with an `onLinkDiagnostics` callback once per assembled export. No target requests are made during rendering. Network/consistency failures still fail a build. Migration 0010 must precede the matching engine; roll back with matching artifacts and the matching SQLite/D1 backup. Populated model removal remains prohibited.

# Docker Compose development

Run Lace on your own machine: the packaged API/admin and MinIO in Docker Compose, operator commands on the host.

**Working directory:** the CMS installation root that contains `package.json`, `lace.config.ts` and this `docs/` directory (for example `cms/`). Run every command from there.

**Result:** a running local CMS with a first administrator, published content and a read-only build token.

Site mode: **starter**. The editable Astro site is `site/`; you also run its development server and a static build.

## Prerequisites

- Node `>=24.12.0` and pnpm `>=12` (tested baseline: Node `24.12.0`, the project-pinned pnpm `12.3.4`).
- Docker with Compose and a running daemon. MinIO's first image build needs network access and disk space.
- Lace `0.1.0-rc2` or a later compatible release of the packages in `package.json` and the API/builder images in `.env.example`.

## Install and prepare the environment

One-time:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm env:prepare
```

Preparation creates a protected, ignored `.env` with random auth, MinIO and builder credentials and an empty `LACE_BUILD_TOKEN`. It prints no secrets and refuses to overwrite an existing `.env`; keep and review an existing one instead. Never commit `.env`. Details and recovery: [environment preparation](lace-operations.md#prerequisites-and-generation).

Review `.env` before any command that loads it. Change only what your machine needs:

- `LACE_API_IMAGE` and `LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE`: compatible image references for your Lace release.
- `LACE_API_PORT` and `LACE_HTTP_PORT`: host ports for the API/admin and the static web proxy.
- `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and `LACE_API_BASE_URL`: both default to `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`. Change both when you change the API port. Use the exact public origin for admin login (`localhost` and `127.0.0.1` differ). Keep path prefixes and the trailing slash.

Keep every generated credential.

## Prepare the database and start the CMS

The host commands `pnpm db:migrate`, `pnpm content:sync` and `pnpm auth:bootstrap` open the same SQLite file as the Compose `api` and `dispatcher` services. Run them only while those services are stopped. The CLI now checks Docker storage mappings before opening SQLite and refuses access while a Compose container uses that file. This protects the maintenance window: on Docker Desktop and OrbStack the data directory crosses a virtual-machine file share that does not share SQLite locks, and a host command run against a running stack can stop publications from triggering builds until the services restart. On the first run nothing is running yet.

One-time, in this order:

```bash
pnpm exec lace doctor --target node --mode compose --stage setup
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm content:sync
pnpm auth:bootstrap
pnpm dev:api
```

- Doctor is read-only. During `setup`, a missing database, unavailable API and empty build token are `expected`; correct every `fail` first. See [doctor limits and exit codes](lace-operations.md#read-only-environment-checks).
- Migration is explicit and creates `.lace/data/` when missing; the API never migrates on startup.
- Sync registers Home and Posts and creates the Home draft.
- Bootstrap prints one setup token that expires after one hour. Capture it privately.
- `pnpm dev:api` starts MinIO, its initialization, the migration service and the API/admin. Wait until `/health/ready` at your API origin answers `ready`.

## Create the first administrator

Open `/admin/` at your `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:3000/admin/`). While setup is incomplete the browser shows the setup screen: enter your email, a password of 12–1024 characters and the bootstrap token, create the administrator, then sign in. After an interruption, retry with the same token and email.

The API alternative sends `POST /api/v1/setup/admin` with exactly `token`, `email` and `password`. This request uses placeholders only: replace `<PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL>` with your configured `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, including any path prefix and its trailing slash, use the token just issued by bootstrap and a password of at least 12 characters.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --request POST \
  '<PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL>api/v1/setup/admin' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"token":"<SETUP_TOKEN>","email":"<ADMIN_EMAIL>","password":"<PASSWORD_AT_LEAST_12_CHARACTERS>"}'
```

Replacing inline placeholders with real credentials exposes them in shell history and process arguments. Prefer the [private-input setup script](lace-operations.md#migrate-sync-and-create-the-first-administrator), which prompts without recording credentials.

If an unused token expired, stop the services (`docker compose stop api dispatcher`), run `pnpm auth:bootstrap` again and start them with `pnpm dev:api`. Successful setup consumes the token and closes setup (later requests return 404); sign in with the existing administrator instead. A setup token is neither a password nor a build token.

## Issue a build token

In Admin Settings create a read-only build token and put its one-time value into `LACE_BUILD_TOKEN` in `.env`. It reads published exports only. Keep it server-side: never in `VITE_*`, `LACE_PUBLIC_*`, browser code, HTML or source control. Replace an expired or revoked token through Settings.

## Publish content

In Admin open Home, set a title, add blocks, save the draft and publish as the administrator. Upload images through Media and select them in image or hero blocks. For a blog page create a Posts entry with a title and a valid slug, then publish. Editors save drafts; publication requires an administrator. With compatible current artifacts, reordered, inserted and duplicated blocks save and publish in the order the editor shows. Site-wide text lives in globals under Site: open Site settings, set the site name and tagline and publish; the starter header shows static values until then.

Saving a draft never changes published content or requests a build.

## Run and build the site

With `LACE_BUILD_TOKEN` set:

```bash
pnpm dev
pnpm build
pnpm typecheck
```

- `pnpm dev` serves the editable site, normally at `http://localhost:4321/`. After a publication, reload: dev revalidates the published export, so changes to `/` and existing posts appear without a restart. Restart dev for a new or renamed slug (Astro caches static paths) or after token/environment changes; this is an Astro limitation, not a Lace defect.
- `pnpm build` reads one authenticated published export and writes `site/dist/`. Publish Home first. Publication alone never changes an existing `site/dist/` and Lace does not deploy a manual build: run a fresh build and deploy it with your own host.
- Missing or rejected tokens, an unavailable API, unpublished Home and unknown blocks fail with corrective messages.

## Repeat and restart

Daily start and stop:

```bash
pnpm dev:api
pnpm dev:stop
```

Stopping preserves `.lace/data/` and the MinIO volume. Restarting needs no migration, sync or bootstrap.

After editing `lace.config.ts`, or for any other host database command, stop the services first, run the command and start again:

```bash
docker compose stop api dispatcher
pnpm content:sync --check
pnpm content:sync
pnpm dev:api
```

`--check` reports pending or incompatible changes without writing. Incompatible structural changes to populated models are blocked; see [configuration, routes, renderers and styling](lace-operations.md#configuration-routes-renderers-and-styling). After upgrading Lace packages or images, run `pnpm db:migrate` the same way.

## Recovery

- **Doctor fails.** Follow each check's next action; exit `4` is compatibility or settings, `5` migration state, `6` infrastructure.
- **Login fails.** Use the exact `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` origin; `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are different origins.
- **Publications stop triggering builds after a host command.** Stop and restart `api` and `dispatcher` as shown above.
- **Destructive reset.** Removing `.lace/data/` or Compose volumes deletes content, accounts and media. Back up first; use it only for disposable data.

## Next steps

- Run the CMS, builder and static web proxy on a server: [Docker Compose production](lace-compose-production.md).
- See when each mode shows a publication: [when published content becomes visible](lace-operations.md#when-published-content-becomes-visible).

- Extend models, routes and blocks: [configuration, routes, renderers and styling](lace-operations.md#configuration-routes-renderers-and-styling).

## Backup, rotation and observation

Follow [Operator observation and recovery](lace-operations.md#operator-observation-and-recovery) for the CMS release card, health/log meanings, coordinated database/object backup, isolated restore, credential rotation and migration/upgrade recovery. Verify the whole restored site before trusting a backup. Remote account operations remain owner-operated.

## Optional API documentation UI

For a Lace release containing the API documentation UI, set
`LACE_API_DOCS_ENABLED=true` in `.env` and recreate the API container with
`docker compose up -d --force-recreate api`. Open `/api/docs` on your API origin.
The page is public when enabled; interactive requests keep normal API permission,
validation and concurrency checks and use existing same-origin sessions. The
browser needs `cdn.jsdelivr.net` access for a pinned Scalar script. No external
request proxy or prefilled/persisted credentials are configured; telemetry,
remote fonts and optional hosted integrations are disabled.

Absent or exact `false` disables the page (API `404`); other values, including an
empty string, are invalid. `/api/v1/openapi.json` remains available. Set `false`
and recreate the container again to disable.

# Docker Compose production

Run Lace on a server with Docker Compose: the packaged API/admin, MinIO, the dispatcher, the fixed-command builder and the web proxy, from the same managed files as development.

**Working directory:** the CMS installation root on the server that contains `package.json`, `lace.config.ts` and this `docs/` directory (for example `cms/`). Run every command from there.

**Result:** the CMS at your public origin, and a static site served by the web proxy after each successful fixed-command build. Publication queues a build; a failed build keeps the previous release online.

Site mode: **starter**. The builder builds the generated `site/` (source root `.`, site directory `site`).

This guide does not depend on the development guide; it repeats the one-time initialization because production uses its own `.env`, origins and data.

## Prerequisites

- A server with Docker, Compose and a running daemon, plus Node `>=24.12.0` and pnpm `>=12` for the host operator commands (tested baseline: Node `24.12.0`, pnpm `12.3.4`).
- Compatible API and builder images for your Lace release (`0.1.0-rc2` or a later compatible release). Pin exact tags or digests; the packages in `package.json` must come from the same release.
- A public HTTPS origin and a TLS-terminating reverse proxy that forwards to `LACE_HTTP_PORT`. The web proxy routes `/admin`, `/api/` and `/health/` to the API and everything else to the static site, so one origin can serve both.

- A committed `pnpm-lock.yaml` at this root: the builder installs `site/` with a frozen lockfile from the read-only source mount.

## Install and prepare the environment

One-time:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm env:prepare
```

Preparation creates a protected `.env` with fresh random `LACE_AUTH_SECRET`, MinIO and builder credentials. It refuses to overwrite an existing `.env`. Never copy a development `.env` to production; back up `.env` privately, because losing `LACE_AUTH_SECRET` invalidates sessions and losing MinIO credentials blocks media access.

Review `.env`:

- `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`: the public HTTPS origin users and browsers reach, with a trailing slash, for example `https://cms.example.com/`. Admin login, authentication and rendered media URLs use it.
- `LACE_API_BASE_URL`: the origin host commands and manual Astro builds use for the authenticated export. The Compose builder always uses the internal `http://api:3000/`.
- `LACE_API_IMAGE` and `LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE`: the exact compatible images.
- `LACE_API_PORT` and `LACE_HTTP_PORT`: host ports. Expose only your reverse proxy publicly and restrict direct access to these ports.

- Build site: `LACE_BUILD_SOURCE_ROOT`, `LACE_BUILD_SITE_DIR`, `LACE_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR`, `LACE_BUILD_SITE_ID` and `LACE_BUILD_SITE_LABEL` select what the builder builds; see [Selecting the build site](lace-operations.md#selecting-the-build-site).
- Site output: set `LACE_BUILD_SITE_URL` to the public site URL so pages get canonical URLs and the build writes `sitemap.xml`; set `LACE_SITE_INDEXING=off` on a staging installation to keep it out of search engines.

## Initialize the CMS

Host database commands share the SQLite file with the Compose `api` and `dispatcher` services: run them only while those services are stopped (see the [development guide](lace-compose-dev.md#prepare-the-database-and-start-the-cms)). On a fresh server nothing runs yet.

One-time:

```bash
pnpm exec lace doctor --target node --mode compose --stage setup
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm content:sync
pnpm auth:bootstrap
pnpm dev:api
```

`pnpm dev:api` starts only MinIO, the migration service and the API/admin, so you can create the administrator before the builder needs a token. Bootstrap prints one setup token that expires after one hour.

Open `<LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>admin/`, create the first administrator on the setup screen with the bootstrap token and sign in. To avoid putting credentials in shell history, use the browser or the [private-input setup script](lace-operations.md#migrate-sync-and-create-the-first-administrator). In Settings create a read-only build token and put its one-time value into `LACE_BUILD_TOKEN` in `.env`; never expose it to browsers.

## Start the full stack

```bash
pnpm prod:start
docker compose ps
```

Wait until `docker compose ps` lists every service as running (`healthy` where a health check exists) and `/health/ready` at your public origin answers `ready`.

`pnpm prod:start` recreates the services with the build token and starts the dispatcher, the fixed-command builder and the web proxy. The builder mounts the selected source read-only, runs a frozen install and `astro build`, and switches the served release only after a complete static output exists. Publication queues a build; request one in Builds if an earlier publication was already processed. Only **Succeeded** proves the release switched; the new release can be served a moment before Builds records it. Browsers revalidate pages because the proxy sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`; the content-hashed files under `/_astro/` (scripts, styles and image variants) are cached for 30 days instead. The builder keeps the pnpm store and the Astro image cache in the `builder-cache` volume, so later builds download and convert only what changed; it clears that cache above 2 GiB and drops the Astro part after a failed build.

While the services run, `/health/ready` is the readiness authority: the API keeps SQLite in write-ahead-log mode, which doctor's `ready` stage refuses to inspect, so it reports the database as unavailable. To run it, stop the database users and switch the journal mode first as described in [doctor limits](lace-operations.md#read-only-environment-checks).

## Configure email (optional)

Account email is disabled until you set `LACE_EMAIL_PROVIDER` in `.env`. Use `smtp` with STARTTLS or implicit TLS, or `resend` with `LACE_RESEND_API_KEY`, plus `LACE_EMAIL_FROM`; see [Email delivery](lace-operations.md#email-delivery). Run `pnpm exec lace doctor --target node --mode compose`, recreate the API with `docker compose up -d --force-recreate api`, then send a test from Settings → Email delivery.

## Repeat operations

After editing `lace.config.ts` or upgrading packages/images, stop the database users, run the explicit command and start again:

```bash
docker compose stop api dispatcher
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm content:sync
pnpm prod:start
```

`pnpm content:sync --check` previews changes without writing. To change images, update `LACE_API_IMAGE` and `LACE_BUILDER_IMAGE` together with the matching packages, then run the sequence above.

Backups: with `api` and `dispatcher` stopped, copy `.lace/data/` (the SQLite database) and back up the MinIO data volume with your volume tooling, together with `.env`. `pnpm prod:stop` stops everything and keeps `.lace/data/`, MinIO and static-output volumes. Never use `docker compose down --volumes` on production data.

## Recovery

- **Build failed.** Builds shows a sanitized cause, its correction and, for source problems, a source entry relative to the installation root (for example a rejected symbolic link, an unreadable or missing entry, a frozen-install failure or an Astro build error). The previous complete release stays online and the publication stays committed. Correct the source, lockfile or settings and use **Retry build**; automatic retries stop after eight attempts. Details: [builder source diagnostics](lace-operations.md#builder-source-diagnostics).
- **Reset the build cache.** Run `docker compose rm --stop --force builder`, remove the `<project>_builder-cache` volume with `docker volume rm` and start the builder again with `pnpm prod:start`. The next build downloads packages and converts every image again.
- **Builder cannot see the source.** Correct the host bind and permissions for `LACE_BUILD_SOURCE_ROOT`, then `docker compose up -d --force-recreate api dispatcher builder`.

- **Setup token expired.** Stop `api` and `dispatcher`, run `pnpm auth:bootstrap` again, start with `pnpm dev:api` and retry. After setup completes, bootstrap refuses; sign in instead.
- **Login or media URLs use the wrong host.** Correct `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and the reverse proxy, then recreate the services.
- **Publications stop triggering builds after a host command.** Restart `api` and `dispatcher`.

## Next steps

- Extend models, routes and blocks: [configuration, routes, renderers and styling](lace-operations.md#configuration-routes-renderers-and-styling).

- Understand when visitors see a publication: [when published content becomes visible](lace-operations.md#when-published-content-becomes-visible).

## Trusted client identity

The API ignores forwarding headers unless its immediate TCP peer matches
`LACE_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` (comma-separated IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs). Empty is the secure
default: clients behind one proxy share the authentication/setup IP limit. Upload
and token-management limits use the authenticated user even behind a shared proxy.
Better Auth and Lace use the same resolved client identity. Missing transport
identity uses a conservative shared fallback; arbitrary headers cannot replace it.

Before exposing a proxy deployment, identify the ingress proxy address/subnet on
its isolated Docker network, set only that controlled subnet in your user-owned
`.env`, and recreate `api` and `dispatcher`. Inspect the proxy's network addresses
with `docker inspect --format '{{json .NetworkSettings.Networks}}' <web-container>`;
choose the configured network CIDR, not an unrelated private range. Restrict direct
API ingress so untrusted services cannot impersonate a trusted peer. Do not trust
all addresses or an entire shared corporate/container network. The proxy must
append the observed peer to X-Forwarded-For or replace that header; Lace walks the
chain from the trusted end and stops at the first untrusted address. Hostnames,
ports and malformed chains are not client addresses. Local TLS/proxy tests do not
confirm your deployed ingress configuration.

Upgrading a template never edits your `.env`; add this setting explicitly when
needed. On Cloudflare the Worker ingress uses the edge-supplied CF-Connecting-IP;
direct calls to the internal runtime do not establish that trust. Restrict any
same-zone Worker subrequests that can rewrite client-IP headers at your ingress.

## Backup, rotation and observation

Follow [Operator observation and recovery](lace-operations.md#operator-observation-and-recovery) for the CMS release card, health/log meanings, coordinated database/object backup, isolated restore, credential rotation and migration/upgrade recovery. Verify the whole restored site before trusting a backup. Remote account operations remain owner-operated.

## Optional API documentation UI

For a Lace release containing the API documentation UI, set
`LACE_API_DOCS_ENABLED=true` in `.env` and recreate the API container with
`docker compose up -d --force-recreate api`. Open `/api/docs` on your API origin.
The page is public when enabled; interactive requests keep normal API permission,
validation and concurrency checks and use existing same-origin sessions. The
browser needs `cdn.jsdelivr.net` access for a pinned Scalar script. No external
request proxy or prefilled/persisted credentials are configured; telemetry,
remote fonts and optional hosted integrations are disabled.

Absent or exact `false` disables the page (API `404`); other values, including an
empty string, are invalid. `/api/v1/openapi.json` remains available. Set `false`
and recreate the container again to disable.

# Optional content assistant

MCP is disabled by default. Apply the release's checked-in database migrations,
then set `LACE_MCP_ENABLED=true` in the Node API environment or Worker vars and
restart/redeploy. Local Worker development uses `worker/.dev.vars`. No new
Cloudflare binding is needed. Other values except `false` are rejected.

Use the canonical API origin configured by `LACE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, with HTTPS
in production. Connect a Streamable HTTP OAuth client to `/mcp`. Discovery is
available at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` and
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth`. Public clients register at
`/api/auth/oauth2/register` and use authorization code with S256 PKCE.

Sign in with the existing Lace account and explicitly approve read access or
draft editing or publishing. Read is the default; only administrators can grant
`content:publish` (which includes read and write). Model discovery, list, get,
create, save draft and `publish_entry` are available according to the grant.
Unpublishing, deletion and media administration remain unavailable, including
for administrators. The current role still applies; demotion removes publication
on the next request. Published content reaches the site with the next build.

Manage your own connections under Account. Access tokens expire within fifteen
minutes. Refresh requires `offline_access`, rotates on use and expires within
thirty days of the grant. Replaying a consumed refresh token revokes its family;
reconnect after a lost refresh response. Account disable, password reset,
sign-out-everywhere and revoke-others invalidate delegated authority. Ordinary
browser sign-out leaves independent connections intact.

After an uncertain create/save result, re-read content. Do not automatically
create another entry or overwrite a draft using a newly loaded revision.

Set `LACE_MCP_ENABLED=false` to disable discovery, issuance, refresh and MCP use.
Keep the additive migrations and stored connection records. Re-enabling does
not reactivate revoked authority. Local test evidence is separate from acceptance
of your actual Node/Cloudflare deployment.

## Inspect configuration and connect Codex

Admin **Settings → MCP** always shows the server-confirmed Enabled/Disabled
configuration and canonical endpoint, including while MCP is disabled. Refresh
status reloads it; a failed refresh labels the last values as stale. Enabled
means the deployment enables MCP, not that an external client has connected.
The section offers endpoint copying, Codex CLI/TOML, Claude Code and Gemini CLI
examples, and generic Streamable HTTP/OAuth guidance. Read only is selected by default; draft editing
adds write scope; Publishing adds write and publish. **Account** lists and revokes your own connections when enabled.

For the default local endpoint, run on the computer running Codex:

```sh
codex mcp add lace --url 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp'
codex mcp login lace --oauth-client-registration dcr --scopes content:read,offline_access
```

To request draft editing, use:

```sh
codex mcp login lace --oauth-client-registration dcr --scopes content:read,content:write,offline_access
```

An alternative configuration in `~/.codex/config.toml` is:

```toml
[mcp_servers.lace]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp"
scopes = ["content:read", "offline_access"]
```

Then run the OAuth login command above. Use your Settings endpoint instead of
the example if your origin or port differs. If `lace` is already configured,
update that entry instead of adding a duplicate. Sign in through the browser,
approve consent, and restart/reload your client to pick up configuration.
Selecting different scopes in Settings grants nothing by itself; an existing
connection needs new consent for additional write or publish authority. To replace a connection, revoke it in
Account and repeat OAuth login. Viewers cannot grant write access. Only administrators can grant publishing.
Unpublishing and deletion remain unavailable. This guidance does not establish
acceptance of any particular external client release.

### Claude Code

For read-only access, run in your terminal:

```sh
claude mcp add-json --scope user lace '{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp","oauth":{"scopes":"content:read offline_access"}}'
```

`--scope user` selects user-level client configuration, not Lace permissions.
Inside Claude Code, run `/mcp`, select `lace`, and authenticate with your Lace
account in the browser. For draft editing, use
`"scopes":"content:read content:write offline_access"` in the server definition
and authenticate again for new write consent. If `lace` already exists, update
its configuration rather than running add-json again. Keep unrelated settings.
See [Claude Code's official MCP guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

### Gemini CLI

Merge the following read-only entry into `~/.gemini/settings.json`, preserving
other settings and updating an existing `lace` entry instead of duplicating it:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lace": {
      "httpUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp",
      "oauth": {
        "enabled": true,
        "scopes": ["content:read", "offline_access"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Inside an interactive Gemini CLI session, run `/mcp auth lace` and approve
browser sign-in with your Lace account. This is separate from signing in to the
CLI's model provider. For draft editing, add `"content:write"` to the scopes
array and authenticate again. Gemini uses an array of scopes; Claude Code uses
a space-separated string. Both use discovery and public-client registration;
no client secret or manual bearer token is needed. Replace the sample endpoint
with the canonical URL in Settings and restart/reload your client after changes.
These recipes follow the [official Gemini CLI MCP guide](https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/mcp-server/);
they do not describe the consumer Gemini web app or claim a verified client login.
Lace role limits, explicit consent and the unpublish/delete ban still apply.

## Publishing and reconnecting

Choose Publishing in Settings. Use these scopes in the selected client recipe:

```sh
codex mcp login lace --oauth-client-registration dcr --scopes content:read,content:write,content:publish,offline_access
```

```toml
[mcp_servers.lace]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp"
scopes = ["content:read", "content:write", "content:publish", "offline_access"]
```

Claude Code's OAuth string is `"scopes":"content:read content:write content:publish offline_access"`.
Gemini CLI's OAuth array is `"scopes":["content:read","content:write","content:publish","offline_access"]`.
Keep the canonical endpoint from Settings and merge existing configuration.
Re-authorize explicitly as an administrator. Existing grants and refresh tokens
never gain publication automatically; HTTP 403 `insufficient_scope` naming
`content:publish` means new consent is needed. No new database migration.

`publish_entry` takes `entryId`, required `expectedRevision` and optional
`idempotencyKey` with the REST header syntax. It publishes the stored draft through
the same validation, revision, route and internal-link guards. Keep the same key,
entry and revision when retrying an uncertain response. The shared REST-shaped
result is `{entry, publication, build}`; replay reports `replayed` and a
`not-dispatched` build without a second publication. Builds coalesce and content
reaches the site on the next build. Unpublish and delete remain forbidden.
A leaked publish-scoped token can change public content; review and revoke
connections under Account.
